simulator_description: This simulator models a single-stage Beer Game supply chain where, at each discrete time step, on-hand inventory is increased by shipments arriving from an order pipeline with stochastic lead times, then reduced by fulfilling stochastic customer demand, with any unmet demand accumulating as backlog; new orders (actions) are appended to the pipeline as future shipments. The state is therefore naturally represented by (inventory, backlog, a FIFO-like list of pipeline entries with remaining lead times, and time), and the step logic conserves flow by shipping at most what is available and carrying the remainder as backlog. Demand is generated as a nonnegative count using an overdispersed (Gamma-Poisson) process with a mostly time-driven mean plus weak, bounded conditioning on current backlog and pipeline length to reduce systematic drift when calibrating from limited data, while preserving insertion order in the pipeline avoids altering queue semantics; a small set of “update conventions” (different within-step orderings of arrivals, demand, and ordering) is selected per trajectory to reflect plausible bookkeeping variations without changing the core dynamics.
